cashTip: Carry baht for street food, songthaews and markets; cards work in malls and hotels.
name: Pattaya
tagline: Bangkok's beach city of temples, islands and nightlife
summary: Pattaya is Thailand's closest big beach resort to Bangkok. Beyond its famous nightlife, it has the astonishing all-wood Sanctuary of Truth, island boat trips to Koh Larn, floating markets, theme parks and a breezy seafront.
seasonNote: November to February is dry and breezy. March to May is hot; the rainy season brings afternoon showers.
arrival: About 2 hours by road from Bangkok's Suvarnabhumi Airport; U-Tapao Airport is 40 minutes south.
gettingAround: Baht-bus songthaews loop the main roads for 10 baht; Grab for longer trips.
foodTip: Seafood at Naklua and Jomtien, and som tam from street stalls.
buyTip: Night markets like Thepprasit for clothes and snacks.
baseArea: Jomtien or Naklua for calm; Central Pattaya for nightlife

items.name: Sanctuary of Truth
items.summary: A vast seaside temple carved entirely from wood, still under construction.
items.expect: Hard hats in work zones; dress modestly.
items.tip: Go late afternoon for warm light on the carvings.

items.name: Koh Larn
items.summary: Coral Island's clear water and sandy bays, 45 minutes by ferry.
items.expect: Cheap public ferries from Bali Hai pier.
items.tip: Rent a scooter or songthaew to Samae Beach.

items.name: Big Buddha Hill
items.summary: A golden seated Buddha on the hill between Pattaya and Jomtien.
items.expect: Free; stairs flanked by naga serpents.

items.name: Nong Nooch Garden
items.summary: Huge themed tropical gardens with shows and dinosaur sculptures.

items.name: Walking Street
items.summary: Pattaya's neon nightlife strip of bars, clubs and shows.

items.name: Pattaya Floating Market
items.summary: Wooden market houses over a lake, with boats selling food and crafts.
items.why: Four regions of Thailand in one place.

items.name: Pratumnak viewpoint
items.summary: The famous Pattaya City sign and bay views.

items.name: Naklua seafood
items.summary: Seafood restaurants on stilts at Lan Pho market.

items.name: Street food
items.summary: Som tam, grilled pork skewers and mango sticky rice.

items.name: Thepprasit night market
items.summary: A weekend night market of snacks and stalls.

cashTip: Cards and Grab work widely; carry ringgit for night markets and hawker stalls.
name: Langkawi
tagline: Duty-free islands of rainforest and beaches
summary: Langkawi is an archipelago of 99 islands off Malaysia's northwest coast, a UNESCO Global Geopark of ancient rainforest, limestone mangroves and calm beaches. Ride the cable car to the curving Sky Bridge, kayak mangroves and island-hop at sunset.
seasonNote: December to March is driest. May to October brings rain but fewer visitors.
arrival: Flights from Kuala Lumpur take an hour; ferries from Penang take about 3 hours.
gettingAround: No public buses; rent a car or scooter, or use Grab.
foodTip: Nasi kandar, seafood at Kuah and laksa Langkawi.

items.name: SkyCab and Sky Bridge
items.summary: A steep cable car up Gunung Machinchang to a curved bridge over the rainforest.
items.expect: Closes in bad weather; long queues midday.

items.name: Kilim Karst Geoforest
items.summary: Boat trips through mangroves and limestone, with eagles and bat caves.

items.name: Pantai Cenang
items.summary: The main beach strip with sunsets, cafés and watersports.

items.name: Island hopping
items.summary: Boats to the Lake of the Pregnant Maiden, eagle watching and Beras Basah beach.

items.name: Seven Wells Waterfall
items.summary: A tiered waterfall with natural pools in the forest.

items.name: Tanjung Rhu beach
items.summary: A calm, quieter beach with limestone islets.
items.tip: Wade to the islets at low tide.

items.name: Night markets
items.summary: A different village hosts a night market each evening.
items.tip: Ask your hotel where tonight's is.

items.name: Seafood restaurants
items.summary: Chilli crab and grilled fish at seafront restaurants.

items.name: Laksa Langkawi
items.summary: A fish-broth laksa eaten with thick rice noodles.

cashTip: Cards and Grab work widely; carry ringgit for night markets and hawker stalls.
name: Malacca
tagline: A crossroads of empires on the Malacca Strait
summary: Malacca is a UNESCO port city layered with Malay, Portuguese, Dutch, British and Chinese history. Its red Dutch square, Peranakan shophouses on Jonker Street and riverside walks make it Malaysia's most historic weekend escape.
seasonNote: Warm and humid all year. Weekends and holidays are crowded; Jonker Street night market is Friday to Sunday.
arrival: About 2 hours by bus from Kuala Lumpur.
gettingAround: Walk the old town; trishaws (decorated, noisy) and Grab.
foodTip: Chicken rice balls, Nyonya laksa and cendol.
buyTip: Peranakan beaded shoes and antiques on Jonker Street.

items.name: Dutch Square
items.summary: Red Dutch buildings, Christ Church and the Stadthuys.

items.name: Jonker Street
items.summary: Shophouse street of antiques, cafés and a weekend night market.

items.name: St Paul's Hill and A Famosa
items.summary: A ruined Portuguese church on the hill and the last gate of the fort.

items.name: Malacca River cruise
items.summary: Boats past murals, old warehouses and Kampung Morten.

items.name: Cheng Hoon Teng Temple
items.summary: Malaysia's oldest working Chinese temple, from the 1600s.

items.name: Baba and Nyonya Heritage Museum
items.summary: A rich Peranakan family townhouse.

items.name: Chicken rice balls
items.summary: Hainanese chicken with rice shaped into balls.

items.name: Nyonya cuisine
items.summary: Nyonya laksa, ayam pongteh and kuih.

items.name: Cendol
items.summary: Shaved ice with coconut milk, green jelly and gula melaka syrup.

cashTip: Carry rupiah for warungs, becak and temple donations; Grab and Gojek take cards.
name: Yogyakarta
tagline: Java's cultural heart between Borobudur and Prambanan
summary: Yogyakarta is Java's soulful cultural capital, still ruled by a sultan. It's the base for Borobudur, the world's largest Buddhist temple, and the soaring Hindu temples of Prambanan, plus batik, gamelan, puppetry and Mount Merapi.
seasonNote: May to September is dry. Borobudur sunrise is best in the dry season.
arrival: Yogyakarta International Airport is an hour by train; trains from Jakarta take about 7 hours.
gettingAround: Grab and Gojek; becak in the old centre; hire a driver for the temples.
foodTip: Gudeg jackfruit stew, bakpia and angkringan street stalls.

items.name: Borobudur
items.summary: A 9th-century stepped Buddhist monument with 2,600 relief panels.
items.expect: Climbing the upper levels needs a timed ticket with guide and sandals.

items.name: Prambanan
items.summary: Soaring 9th-century Hindu temples to Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma.
items.expect: Sunset is lovely; Ramayana ballet on some nights.
items.tip: Stay for the open-air Ramayana ballet.

items.name: Kraton
items.summary: The sultan's palace with gamelan and dance performances in the mornings.

items.name: Taman Sari
items.summary: The sultan's former water castle with bathing pools and an underground mosque.

items.name: Mount Merapi jeep tour
items.summary: Jeep rides through lava fields of Java's most active volcano.

items.name: Malioboro Street
items.summary: The main street of batik shops and evening street food.

items.name: Jomblang Cave
items.summary: Abseil into a cave where a 'heavenly light' beam shines at midday.

items.name: Gudeg
items.summary: Young jackfruit stewed in palm sugar and coconut milk.

items.name: Angkringan stalls
items.summary: Night stalls of tiny rice packets, satay and kopi joss with charcoal.

items.name: Bakpia
items.summary: Small pastries filled with mung bean.

cashTip: Carry rupees for tuk-tuks, temples and street food; cards work in hotels and bigger restaurants.
name: Colombo
tagline: Sri Lanka's seaside capital of temples and food
summary: Colombo is Sri Lanka's busy seaside capital and the gateway to the island. Walk Galle Face Green at sunset, see Gangaramaya and the island-temple Seema Malaka, browse Pettah's markets and eat superb hoppers and crab.
seasonNote: December to March is driest on the west coast; May to September brings the southwest monsoon.
arrival: Bandaranaike Airport is about an hour north.
gettingAround: Tuk-tuks via PickMe or Uber; trains along the coast.
foodTip: Hoppers, kottu and Ministry of Crab.
buyTip: Tea, spices and handloom at Barefoot.

items.name: Gangaramaya Temple
items.summary: An eclectic temple-museum crowded with statues and gifts.

items.name: Seema Malaka
items.summary: A floating temple by Geoffrey Bawa on Beira Lake.

items.name: Galle Face Green
items.summary: A seafront promenade full of kites and street food at sunset.

items.name: Pettah markets
items.summary: Chaotic bazaar streets and the red-and-white Jami Ul-Alfar Mosque.
items.tip: Visit the mosque outside prayer time.

items.name: National Museum
items.summary: Sri Lanka's history, from royal regalia to ancient art.

items.name: Number 11, Geoffrey Bawa's house
items.summary: The architect's own house, a maze of courtyards.

items.name: Hoppers
items.summary: Bowl-shaped rice pancakes, best with an egg in the middle.

items.name: Kottu roti
items.summary: Chopped roti stir-fried with vegetables and meat, to a metal clatter.

items.name: Lagoon crab
items.summary: Giant Sri Lankan crabs in pepper or garlic.

cashTip: Carry rupees for tuk-tuks, temples and street food; cards work in hotels and bigger restaurants.
name: Galle
tagline: A Dutch fort town on Sri Lanka's southern coast
summary: Galle's 17th-century Dutch fort is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, with ramparts, a lighthouse, colonial streets and boutique cafés. It's the base for beaches at Unawatuna and Mirissa, whale watching and stilt fishermen.
seasonNote: December to April is the south coast's dry season; whale season runs roughly November to April.
arrival: About 2 hours from Colombo by expressway or a scenic coastal train.
gettingAround: Walk the fort; tuk-tuks along the coast.
foodTip: Fish curry and rice, and seafood at the beaches.

items.name: Galle Fort
items.summary: Walk the ramparts and colonial lanes of a still-lived-in Dutch fort.

items.name: Lighthouse and Flag Rock
items.summary: The fort's white lighthouse and cliff-jumpers at Flag Rock.

items.name: Unawatuna beach
items.summary: A curved bay with calm water and snorkelling.

items.name: Mirissa whale watching
items.summary: Blue whales and dolphins off the south coast.

items.name: Stilt fishermen at Koggala
items.summary: Fishermen perched on poles in the surf.
items.expect: Many are posed for photos and ask for tips.

items.name: Maritime Museum
items.summary: Inside the old Dutch warehouse.
flow: See the ship models and trade exhibits.

items.name: Rice and curry
items.summary: Rice with half a dozen curries, sambols and papadum.

items.name: Beach seafood
items.summary: Grilled catch of the day on the beach.

items.name: Fort cafés
items.summary: Colonial-house cafés serving tea and cakes.

cashTip: Resorts bill in US dollars to your room; carry some USD or rufiyaa for local islands and tips.
name: Malé · Maldives
tagline: Turquoise atolls, coral reefs and overwater villas
summary: The Maldives is a nation of 1,190 coral islands in 26 atolls, famous for turquoise lagoons, house reefs, manta rays and overwater villas. Fly into Malé, then reach resorts or local islands by speedboat or seaplane.
seasonNote: December to April is the dry northeast monsoon. May to November is wetter but good for mantas and whale sharks in some atolls.
arrival: Velana International Airport is on its own island next to Malé.
gettingAround: Speedboats, seaplanes and public ferries; resorts arrange transfers.
foodTip: Mas huni tuna breakfast, garudhiya fish soup and hedhikaa snacks.
buyTip: Lacquer work, mats and local tuna products.
baseArea: A resort, or Maafushi for a budget local island

items.name: Snorkelling the house reef
items.summary: Reefs right off the beach, with turtles, rays and reef sharks.

items.name: Manta and whale shark trips
items.summary: Swim with whale sharks in South Ari or mantas in Baa Atoll's Hanifaru Bay.
items.tip: Book with a marine biologist-led trip.

items.name: Sandbank picnic
items.summary: A strip of white sand alone in the lagoon.

items.name: Malé city
items.summary: The dense capital, with the Old Friday Mosque of coral stone and a fish market.

items.name: Bioluminescent beaches
items.summary: Glowing plankton lighting the shore on dark nights.

items.name: Maafushi local island
items.summary: A local island with guesthouses, cheap excursions and a bikini beach.

items.name: Mas huni
items.summary: Shredded tuna with coconut, onion and chilli, eaten with roshi flatbread.
items.tip: Ask for it at a local café.

items.name: Garudhiya
items.summary: Clear tuna broth with rice, lime and chilli.

items.name: Resort dinners
items.summary: Beach and overwater dining, often seafood.
